# Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling — facts

> Source-anchored units about Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling: 14 across 6 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## How it works

- [statement] Streaming adds OP_MSG exhaustAllowed to awaitable hello. moreToCome permits successive replies without new requests; drivers process every reply in arrival order and send another awaitable request when a successful reply ends the stream. (low confidence) — https://specifications.readthedocs.io/en/latest/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-monitoring/ · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling
- [statement] [redacted] describes very small pre-auth streamable-hello waits, especially zero, creating rapid server wakeups. The server implementation can clamp a requested wait to minWaitForStreamingHelloMillis or reject it when abortStreamingHelloWithSmallTimeout is enabled; deployments require version-specific verification. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://example.test/withheld-reference · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/replication_info.cpp
- [statement] FaaS suspension can accumulate streamed heartbeats and force clients to process stale responses after resumption. This motivated the polling default; streaming also costs an additional RTT connection and thread per monitored server. (high confidence) — https://specifications.readthedocs.io/en/latest/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-monitoring/ · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-2578, https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-2246

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] AWS documents that Lambda freezes an execution environment once the runtime and extensions finish and no events remain. Unfinished background callbacks or processes resume if Lambda reuses that environment; continuous monitor execution between invocations cannot be assumed. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/us_en/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-runtime-environment.html · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-2578
- [statement] An awaited heartbeat may normally last about ten seconds with the default heartbeat interval. The awaited event field distinguishes intentional server waiting from a slow ordinary heartbeat; duration alone is not network RTT. (low confidence) — https://specifications.readthedocs.io/en/latest/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-monitoring/ · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The FaaS polling default is scoped to supported driver monitoring modes, rather than a claim that streaming is universally unsuitable. Explicit serverMonitoringMode permits an override when platform detection is inaccurate or polling is preferable elsewhere. (high confidence) — https://specifications.readthedocs.io/en/latest/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-monitoring/ · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/blob/master/mongo/options/clientoptions.go

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Awaitable hello is discovered through topologyVersion in a hello response. Requests supply topologyVersion and maxAwaitTimeMS; the server replies on a processId mismatch, a greater topology counter, or expiry of the maximum wait. (high confidence) — https://specifications.readthedocs.io/en/latest/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-monitoring/ · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/replication_info.cpp
- [statement] serverMonitoringMode defaults to auto: detected FaaS uses poll, other environments use stream. Explicit poll forces polling; stream uses streaming only if supported, otherwise polling. Detection follows the handshake client.env rules. (high confidence) — https://specifications.readthedocs.io/en/latest/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-monitoring/ · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/blob/master/mongo/options/clientoptions.go
- [statement] Polling performs hello or legacy hello checks and sleeps heartbeatFrequencyMS between checks. Streaming instead begins the next read immediately after a successful response and sets maxAwaitTimeMS to heartbeatFrequencyMS. (high confidence) — https://specifications.readthedocs.io/en/latest/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-monitoring/ · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/blob/master/mongo/options/clientoptions.go
- [statement] Streaming measures RTT with periodic regular hello commands on a separate dedicated connection; streaming response duration must not update RTT. Polling must not create a dedicated RTT connection. (high confidence) — https://specifications.readthedocs.io/en/latest/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-monitoring/ · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-2578
- [statement] FaaS suspension can accumulate stale streaming heartbeats; DRIVERS-2578 also identifies socket timeouts after runtime resumption as motivation for polling. (high confidence) — https://specifications.readthedocs.io/en/latest/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-monitoring/ · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-2578
- [statement] NODE-6839 records a reconnection complaint after upgrading to Mongoose 8 and driver 6, but its resolution is Gone away with no fix version. It does not establish a confirmed current driver-wide regression. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-03-26) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-6839 · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling
- [statement] Node.js timers define eligibility thresholds, not exact execution times. Starting with libuv 1.45.0 in Node.js 20, timers run after poll in each loop iteration, with a compatibility timer pass before entering the loop. Historical claims that timers always precede socket reads require runtime-specific qualification. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://nodejs.org/en/learn/asynchronous-work/event-loop-timers-and-nexttick · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-6839
- [statement] For awaitable replies, a nonzero connectTimeoutMS becomes a socket timeout of connectTimeoutMS plus heartbeatFrequencyMS. A zero connectTimeoutMS remains unlimited, including awaitable replies. (low confidence) — https://specifications.readthedocs.io/en/latest/server-discovery-and-monitoring/server-monitoring/ · keywords: Awaitable hello streaming monitoring and FaaS polling
